questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/ phrase.

'Barking up the wrong tree.'

options.text: Searching for something in the wrong place.
Training a dog to climb up

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Searching for something in the wrong place.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Barking up the wrong tree (idiom): It means to be pursuing something in the wrong way or focusing on the wrong thing. (गलत रास्ते पर चलना या गलत चीज पर ध्यान देना) 
 
 
• **Example**: "If you think I'm going to lend you money, you're barking up the wrong tree.
 
 
 
• Searching for something in the wrong place: This option accurately captures the essence of the idiom, which is about looking for something where it isn't. (गलत जगह किसी चीज की तलाश करना)
 
 
• **Example:** "I spent hours looking for my keys in the fridge; turns out they were in my pocket all along. 
 
 
 
• Hence, The correct idiom is** 'Searching for something in the wrong place.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 1.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Training a dog to climb up **- This is not the intended meaning of the idiom.
 
• **Following the correct path -** This is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.
 
• **Avoiding confrontation - **This has a different meaning altogether and doesn't relate to pursuing something incorrectly

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

In the early autumn fierce fighting took place, the ______ Serbians bearing a prominent part.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 3'** i.e.** 'Gallant'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, the adjective **"gallant"** describes the Serbians as brave, courageous, or noble, which is a fitting description if they were participating in fierce fighting. This is why this option is the best choice to fill in the blank.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'In the early autumn fierce fighting took place, the** gallant** Serbians bearing a prominent part.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's explain the other options:
 
 
• **"Cowardly" **means lacking courage. It would not make sense to use this word to describe someone who is participating in fierce fighting, as it would imply they are afraid or running away.
 
• **"Unabashed"** means not embarrassed or ashamed, often about something that people might find shocking. This term doesn't fit in the context of the sentence.
 
• **"Bore" **is a verb meaning to make a hole in something, or it can be a noun referring to a person who is dull and uninteresting. Neither of these meanings fits in this context.

questions.question: **Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article. **

options.text: She is a Indian artist married to an European engineer.
She is an Indian artist married to an European engineer.
She is an Indian artist married to a European engineer.
She is a Indian artist married to a European engineer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **She is an Indian artist married to a European engineer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct use of the indefinite article '**a**' is before a noun starting with a consonant sound.
 
• In the given sentence, '**European**' starts with a vowel sound.
 
• Even though "**European**" begins with the letter '**E**,' the sound that follows it is a consonant sound. 
 
• so the correct article to use is '**a**'.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence is "*She is an Indian artist married to a European engineer.*"

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: Incorrect use of the indefinite article 'a' before a noun starting with a vowel sound.
 
• Option 2: Incorrect use of the article 'a' instead of 'an' before a noun starting with a vowel sound.
 
• Option 4: Incorrect use of the indefinite article 'a' before a noun starting with a vowel sound.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Please tell me the truth, / is he here to have been investigating / the murder that / happened across the street?

options.text: is he here to have been investigating

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in option 2 lies in the phrase **"is he here to have been investigating"** which is awkward and incorrectly structured. 
 
• The correct formulation would be **"is he here to investigate."**
 
• The action is not ongoing. It is just asking** whether he is here to investigate the murder.**

**Therefore, the correct sentence is- "*Please tell me the truth, is he here to investigate the murder that happened across the street?"***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("Please tell me the truth,")** is correctly requesting information, setting a polite tone for the question.
 
• **Option 3 ("the murder that")** correctly introduces the subject of the investigation.
 
• **Option 4 ("happened across the street")** provides the location of the event being investigated and is grammatically sound.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rohan exercised and ate a lot, __lest he should not be weak__.

options.text: lest he would not be weak

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structure "lest + subject + should" is used to express a fear or a precaution, and "should" is the correct form in this context.
 
• The phrase "lest he should be weak" correctly follows this construction, conveying that Rohan took actions to prevent weakness.
 
• The other options (such as "lest he would be weak" or "lest he would not be weak") are incorrect because they do not align with the grammatical structure of "lest".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Rohan exercised and ate a lot, lest he should be weak."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "lest he should not weak" – The phrase "should not weak" is grammatically incorrect because "weak" is an adjective, not a verb.
 
• **Option 2:** "lest he would be weak" – The use of "would" is incorrect after "lest"; "should" is the appropriate modal verb in this context.
